subject: [P0] Acme production latency & 5xx spike — mitigation, RCA and ownership
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-platform@acme.com
Date: 2026-09-10T08:03:00Z
Subject: Production search latency and 5xx spike (URGENT)

Karthik —

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and elevated 5xx for the /v1/search API starting ~07:40 UTC this morning. Error rate peaked at 9.8% and P95 latency went from 220ms to ~1.4s for 60+ minutes. This knocked over several critical product flows for us.

Attached is a small sample of the error logs (acme_error_samples.log) and traces for two requests. Our SREs rolled traffic away from the region at 08:15 but we'd like Redwood to confirm root cause and an immediate mitigation plan. Can you confirm:
- Are you aware of any model/serving changes pushed this morning?
- Do you have a mitigation we can apply to bring error rate <1% and P95 <400ms?

This is impacting our customers and we've opened an internal incident; need Redwood on it with exec-level updates.

Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Platform — Acme Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production search latency and 5xx spike (URGENT)

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're kicking off a P0 on our side and will own incident coordination until you confirm otherwise. Initial readouts: no customer-facing config changes were intentionally deployed from Redwood this morning, but our runtime telemetry shows a sudden increase in KV cache evictions and anomalous batching behavior starting at 07:38 UTC.

Immediate actions we're executing now (ETA minutes unless stated):
- Increase pod pool for the search model by +30% in the affected region (Dylan).
- Disable a new quantization fallback that may be causing cache churn (Marissa).
- Enable stricter per-tenant rate shaping for Acme to reduce head-of-line impacts while we stabilize (Karthik).

I've attached our mitigation runbook stub (mitigation-runbook-v1.md) and assigned INF-4821 in Jira. We'll send hourly updates and a preliminary RCA within 24 hours. What SLA remediation process would you like us to trigger now?

Karthik Iyer
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production search latency and 5xx spike (URGENT)

Jordan / team —

Quick technical summary from runtime/serving:
- Timeline: 07:38 UTC — a model runtime path hit an unexpected memory pattern after a pod rehydration event; this increased KV cache misses and caused per-request compute to escalate.
- Root cause (preliminary): a quantization fallback path added in release 20260829 interacts poorly with the new continuous-batching code path under certain sequence-length distributions.
- Impact: higher compute per request -> queueing -> increased latency and transient 5xx under load.

Mitigations applied (08:18–08:45 UTC):
1) Reverted quantization fallback (rolled back patch) — immediate reduction in compute.
2) Increased instance pool + disabled aggressive prefetching for Acme customer shard.
3) Applied temporary per-tenant rate shaping to smooth bursts.

Current status (09:00 UTC): error rate down to 0.9%, P95 ~350ms. We're continuing a controlled capacity ramp and running a soak for 2 hours.

Next steps / owners:
- Full RCA document (Marissa) — delivery by 2026-09-14 EOD.
- Permanent fix in runtime (Engineering) — target 2026-10-01.
- SLA/credit proposal (Sales/Finance) — Hannah to coordinate.

I'll prepare a short exec readout and attach the initial traces.

Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Jordan

Jordan —

I'm really sorry for the disruption — we take outages like this seriously. We'll proceed with the following:

1) Exec summary (one-page) — I'll send a signed note to your CTO by EOD today.
2) SLA remediation: we'll calculate a credit based on the impacted window you provided; finance will produce a formal proposal by 2026-09-13.
3) Post-incident review: Tue 2026-09-15 15:00 UTC works for us; Marissa and two senior engineers will attend.
4) Escalation path: I've opened an internal executive notification and will personally track closure of the action items.

We understand the business impact and will include compensatory measures in our proposal. Thank you to the engineering team for the quick mitigations.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
